is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles arabiensis, a member of the Anopheles gambiae complex (page 1, Abstract).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports genotyping for Vgsc L995F (West African kdr) and Vgsc L995S (East African kdr) (page 1, Abstract; page 2, Table 1).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 1 provides the number of mosquitoes tested, and the counts for homozygote mutation, heterozygote, and homozygote wild type for the West African kdr mutation (page 2).

african_field_population.evidence: The study collected wild-caught adult female Anopheles mosquitoes from 15 villages in southwestern Ethiopia (page 1, Materials and Methods).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study reporting original field collection and molecular analysis of mosquito populations.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study specifies the location as the surroundings of the Gilgel-Gibe hydroelectric dam in southwestern Ethiopia, including village-level data (page 1, Materials and Methods; page 2, Table 1).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The collection period is explicitly stated as September to October 2008 (page 2, Results).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes a specific, localized collection in 2008 and does not indicate it is part of a larger, previously published dataset.

supplement.evidence: All necessary data, including genotype counts and bioassay results, are provided in the main text and tables.

assessment.summary: This study investigated the frequency of kdr mutations in Anopheles arabiensis populations in southwestern Ethiopia. It found a very high frequency of the West African kdr (L995F) mutation (98.5%) and the absence of the East African kdr (L995S) mutation. Bioassays confirmed high resistance to DDT and permethrin.
